gaps.note: The jack part gives led-a the vocabulary link and led-b the vocabulary activity. This switch's right lamp is a status lamp whose meaning follows the mode button, and the upper row is rotated so left and right swap. One group mapping cannot say both.
gaps.wanted: A per-port states mapping that a block can carry, or the jack part split by row.

gaps.note: The hardware guide names the CLD lamp and sends the reader to the cloud-ready LED blink patterns, which are not in this guide.
gaps.wanted: the cloud-ready LED blink patterns and their meanings

gaps.note: The English EX4400 datasheet did not answer from juniper.net and the HPE copy a00150783enw did not either. The French-language datasheet of 2025-10-14 is cited and no figure comes from it.
gaps.wanted: the English EX4400 datasheet, for the ordering part numbers and mounting kit codes

gaps.note: Table 53 gives the 1600 W supply a C15 coupler, which mates a C16 appliance inlet. The registry has only the C14 inlet, which the supply part uses, so the C16 rim is not drawn and a C13 cord would also fit the drawing.
gaps.wanted: a C16 inlet in the connector registry

gaps.note: The spare chassis takes the 2000 W DC supply, juniper/jpsu-2000-c-dc-afo. The guide draws its face only in perspective (Figure 85), so the right half of the face is placed by eye and is estimated. The guide also prints the supply's model number two ways, with and without the C, and the form with the C is used.
gaps.wanted: a render or photograph of the 2000 W DC supply's face

gaps.note: The guide prints EX4400-FAN once, in the switch-tray assembly table, with no airflow direction. No ordering code is stated for the fan modules.
gaps.wanted: the ordering codes of the front-to-back and back-to-front fan modules

gaps.note: The guide states the screw size and lug codes but not the spacing of the two grounding holes. The 15.0 mm spacing is estimated from the render. The holes are drawn as decor, so no two-hole lug can be seated on them.
gaps.wanted: the spacing of the two-hole protective earthing terminal, and a 10-32 pair part for it

gaps.note: The guide sends the reader to the Hardware Compatibility Tool page for EX4400 for the transceivers and cables each port takes, and holds no table of them. The port groups therefore declare no interface.
gaps.wanted: the EX4400 transceiver list from the Hardware Compatibility Tool

gaps.note: The ESD hazard symbol beside the ESD socket and the legends printed on the fan and power supply slot plates are drawn as simple marks. The air-flow word printed on the supply fan hub is not drawn, because no maker figure shows it.
gaps.wanted: a close-up of the rear panel

airflow.note: Table 32 and Table 34 - the 48MP ships only with front-to-back (AFO) fan modules and supply (AIR OUT label, orange handle). No back-to-front 48MP is listed anywhere in the guide. The -S spare ships with no supply and no fan modules, and the guide says the fans to order are AFO.

colour.note: Median of bare face on the guide renders (#777777 at the front, #707070 at the rear), and of the status plate (#50575f) and the jack plate (#cccdcf). The 24X studio photograph shows the same mid-grey finish. The legends of the PoE models are gold (#e8a626) on the render.

extension-slot.note: Figure 43 callout 7. The slot is a recess 363.8 to 437.8 across and 17.7 to 41.2 down in the render of Figure 41, which draws a four-cage module seated; a shipped switch has the cover, because the shipped-components statement under Table 33 names one cover for the empty extension module slot. The slot is a bay and takes the three extension modules the guide names.

gate-1.note: Figure 41 (g022645, 1500 x 199 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a face 1297 px wide (83 to 1379.5) and about 127 px tall, which is 2.936 px per mm across on the stated 441.7 mm and 2.92 down on 43.7 mm. The four jack blocks start at 100, 362, 624 and 886 px, a block step of 89.2 mm, the same as the 48P, and the pitch inside a block is 13.95 mm, the 13.97 mm of the ganged RJ45 registry entry, measured on a quantity the scale never saw. The rear render (Figure 42, the image shared with the 24T and 24P, 2000 x 265 px) gives a face 1733.5 px by 168.5 px, aspect 10.29, 3.92 px per mm across and 3.86 down. Positions are taken per axis on those scales and each reads to about half a millimetre on the front and a quarter on the rear.

grounding.note: Connect Earth Ground to an EX4400 Switch - a 2-hole protective grounding terminal on the rear panel, used with 10-32 x 0.25 in screws and the lugs LCD10-10AF-L, LCD8-10AF-L or LCD6-10AF-L. The guide gives no hole spacing. The 15.0 mm spacing is measured on the render and is estimated. The render shows two bare holes, so they are drawn as dark holes on the plate and not as screws. A two-hole lug is the seat of a pair of holes, and the library has no pair part for 10-32 holes at this spacing, so no lug seat is offered.

interface-names.note: Table 114 - the CLI addresses the switch as FPC 0, the built-in ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 47, the two rear QSFP28 ports as PIC 1 ports 0 and 1, and the extension module as PIC 2. The names are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

model-name.note: The 48MP render (Figure 41) prints "MG PoE++" after EX4400, but its callout drawing (Figure 43) prints "MG PoE+". The 24MP render and callout drawing both print "MG PoE++". The ports deliver 90 W, which is PoE++ in the maker's own naming, so PoE++ is used and the one-plus drawing is taken as a slip.

mounting.note: Mounting Options and the mounting procedures - the two-post kit EX-RMK ships in the box and mounts the brackets flush with the front or along the middle of the side panels. The separately orderable EX-4PST-RMK mounts the switch flush with the front posts of a four-post rack or recessed inside it. EX-WMK is a wall kit. No ear distance in millimetres, no rack depth range and no bracket drawing that can be measured is in the guide, so the positions are named without a number and no kit is listed. The library holds no rail kit yet.

port-leds.note: Figure 50 and Table 43 and Table 44 - each jack has two lamp windows, "1 Link activity LED" at the left and "2 Status LED" at the right, in both rows. The link activity lamp is green: steady for link without traffic, blinking for traffic, unlit for no link. The status lamp shows one port parameter at a time, chosen with the mode button: speed (SPD), duplex (DX), administrative enable (EN) or PoE (POE). On this model the SPD lamp also changes colour - green for 1000 Mbps steady and 100 Mbps blinking, amber for 2.5 Gbps steady and 5 Gbps blinking, blue for 10 Gbps steady. The jack part names its lamps led-a (left when unrotated) and led-b. The upper row is rotated, so left and right swap there. A single mapping for the group would be wrong for one row, so the part keeps its default vocabulary and this note holds the meaning. See the gap port-lamp-vocabulary.

port-numbering.note: Figure 50 (g022608) at high zoom - under each column, one pair of printed numbers, an even number with an up arrow and the next odd number with a down arrow ("0 up 1 down", "2 up 3 down" to "46 up 47 down" on the render). The arrows point at the port of each number, so the upper jack of a column has the even number. Numbering starts at 0, as printed. CLI names (ge-0/0/0 and so on) are not printed on the metal, and Table 114 gives PIC 0 as the built-in ports 0 to 47. The legend position and arrow spacing are estimated from Figure 50 and the render. The legends are gold on the render, as on the other PoE models.

ports.note: Figure 41 and Figure 43 - 48 RJ-45 ports in two rows of 24, in four blocks of six columns with a gutter between them. Cells sit on the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch. The first cell's left edge is at 7.95 mm, the block step is 89.26 mm (so a gutter of 5.44 mm), the upper cells start at 9.5 mm and the lower at 24.05 mm (row step 14.55 mm). Each block is a single silver plate, 87.1 mm wide, 5.71 mm from the left edge for the first, drawn as decor because the metal strip is panel and not part. Figure 43 outlines the fourth block in red as callout 2 - the 12 ports that run to 10 Gbps - and the first three blocks are the 36 that run to 2.5 Gbps, so the face is two port groups and two blocks. Counts confirmed by Table 33 and Table 114 (PIC 0, 36x100M/1G/2.5G Base-T and 12x100M/1G/2.5G/5G/10G Base-T).

power-supplies.note: THE DEFAULT SUPPLY IS 1600 W, NOT 550 W. Table 32 ships the 48MP with a 1600 W AC supply, the text under Figure 44 says the model supports 1600 W AC and 2000 W DC supplies, and Table 90 notes that the 2000 W AC supply is not supported. The rear render shows two supplies and does not tell the ratings apart. This device ships one supply and a cover on the second slot, as Figure 44 and Table 105 show. A bay cannot say that supplies of one chassis must share a rating.

rear.note: Figure 42 and Figure 44 measured on the render, per axis, from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front). CON jack centre 18.35, 13.6; MGMT jack centre 39.6, 13.6, both with the contact comb up; USB-A at 55.0, 12.5, vertical; RESET pinhole at 55.3, 24.9; ground plate 27.8 to 61.7 across and 27.6 to 39.7 down with two threaded holes 15.0 apart at 39.5 and 54.5; QSFP28 cages centred at 75.5 across and 14.5 and 28.2 down, labelled 0 and 1 to their left; two columns of lamps at 89.4 and 94.3 across, two for each cage per row; ESD socket at 101.1, 36.0. Fan module slots are at 108.2 and 206.0 across, and power supply slots at 255.0 and 346.4 across, each with a fan or power icon and its number above the slot or beside it. All of these are estimated from the render, to about 0.3 mm. The guide draws one rear for the 24T, 24P, 48T, 48P, 48F, 24MP and 48MP, and the callout list of Figure 44 is the same as that of the other models.

rear-labels.note: Figure 44 callouts 1, 6, 10 and 15 are the serial number ID label, the CLEI code label, the power supply rating label and the claim code label. They are stickers, not metal, so each is a named region and is not drawn. The render shows them as blank plates, white for three and slate for the rating label. The guide shows no content, and none is invented.

rj45-orientation.note: Figure 50 - upper-row jacks have their contact comb at the bottom and their lamp windows at the top corners, so they carry rotate 180. Lower-row jacks have the comb at the top and the lamps at the bottom corners, the default turn of the part. This is the stacked mirror the registry describes.

sources.note: EX4400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-07-22 (331 pages), fetched from www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4400/ex4400.pdf. Taken from it - Table 4 and Table 7 (the model list), Tables 32 to 34 with Figures 41 to 44 (EX4400-48MP), Table 5 (extension modules), Table 38 to Table 40 (chassis, fan and supply sizes), Tables 41 to 51 (lamps), Table 52 (heat), Tables 53 to 58, 71, 72, 88, 90 and 91 (power supplies and PoE budget), Table 93 (environment), Table 105 (what ships), Table 114 (CLI names) and Table 115 (acoustics). Figure 41 (g022645) and Figure 42 (the rear render shared with the 24T and 24P, g022646) are renders of the real product and are the pictures measured here; Figure 43 (g022556) is the flat callout drawing. Juniper's image library answered for none of the views of this model - the address ex4400-48mp/ex4400-48mp-front-high.jpg returned an HTML 404 page - so the guide's renders are the only picture of each face. The 24X studio photograph, which shares the chassis and the status block, confirms the colour and finish. The EX4400 datasheet on juniper.net (a French-language PDF of 2025-10-14, the only one the site answers for) lists the 48MP as 12 PoE 100M/1/2.5/5/10GbE ports and 36 PoE 100M/1/2.5GbE ports; no figure here comes from it. Terms - Juniper's documentation pages state no licence for the guide, so the facts are transcribed and nothing is copied; no drawing or photograph is in the repository. The held intake folder was not readable by this account, so no earlier photograph, stencil or 3D model could be used. An end-of-life search made 2026-10-20 found no notice for the EX4400 line, so the lifecycle is none-announced.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) - a belly-to-belly pair is the upper cage upright and the lower turned 180, so both bails face outward. The two rear QSFP28 cages are stacked this way and the render at 3.9 px per mm does not resolve which way the latches point, so the rule decides and a photograph overturns it.

status-block.note: Figure 43 callouts 3 to 6 and Figure 54 (g022614), measured on the render of Figure 41. A dark plate 361.2 to 439.5 across and 1.4 to 15.5 down. The model name is printed EX4400 in white from 363.2 mm and MG PoE++ in orange from 375.7 mm. The USB-C console port is centred at 393.7, 8.3 with the USB symbol below it. Two columns of lamps sit at 406.2 and 410.1 across: SYS, ALM, MST and CLD on the left with their legends, and SPD, DX, EN and POE on the right. The rows are at 3.8, 6.8, 9.7 and 12.8 down; the render scatters them by up to 0.5 mm and they are aligned. The mode button is a flush disc at 423.1, 8.6. The legends' type size is estimated.

vents.note: The front has a hexagon punching in a band over and under the port blocks, from the logo to the status block. The rear punching is two small fields above and below the QSFP28 cages. The fields are drawn as a repeating pattern in simplified outlines, not hole for hole.

width.note: Table 33 gives the chassis 17.39 in (44.17 cm) wide, and says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in (48.2 cm). The face is the body between the folds, 441.7 mm, with no ears drawn. Height is 1.72 in (4.37 cm), 1RU. Depth is 15.71 in (39.9 cm) with no supply, fan module or extension module fitted, 16.93 in (43 cm) with a supply and fan modules, 17.35 in (44.07 cm) with an extension module as well. The bare figure 399.0 mm is carried as the chassis depth, because every module is its own part. The other two are in attrs.
